videos.originalDescription:
Full lesson, notes and practice questions: https://hscscience.com.au/subjects/chemistry/year12/module5/lesson11

Two more HSC-style equilibrium questions with traps. Flip K when the vessel starts from the other side of the equation, then use the tiny-K shortcut and check it on 2x, not x. Finally, find K from one mixture and reuse it at the same temperature, where a perfect square is hiding in the question. Each question pauses so you can try it first.

0:00 The two practice questions
0:39 Question 3: flipped and tiny K
1:17 Solve question 3
3:44 Question 4a: find K
5:13 Question 4b: reuse K
7:20 Choose the first move
7:53 Key notes

Chemistry 2017: Year 12 Module 5, Equilibrium and Acid Reactions. Supports performing calculations to find Keq and the concentrations of substances in an equilibrium system.
Syllabus dotpoint (NSW Chemistry Stage 6, 2017, Module 5):
"perform calculations to find the value of Keq and concentrations of substances within an equilibrium system, and use these values to make predictions on the direction in which a reaction may proceed (ACSCH096)"
Official 2017 course: https://www.nsw.gov.au/education-and-training/nesa/curriculum/science/chemistry-stage-6-2017

Prerequisite: Hard HSC equilibrium calculation practice, part 1. Next: How temperature changes K.

videos.originalDescription:
Full lesson, notes and practice questions: https://hscscience.com.au/subjects/chemistry/year12/module5/lesson18

When two ionic solutions are mixed, the final volume dilutes both sets of ions. Calculate the new concentrations, build Qsp and compare it with a reference Ksp to predict a precipitate. Then use the same comparison to explain why a common ion makes a salt less soluble.

0:00 The precipitation question
0:26 Qsp and Ksp
1:19 Mixing dilutes every ion
1:42 Calcium sulfate example
2:48 A second mixing calculation
4:02 Dilute, calculate, compare
4:11 The common ion effect
4:51 ICE table with a common ion
5:33 Solve and check
6:01 Practice question 1
6:38 Answer 1
7:13 Practice question 2
7:43 Answer 2
8:41 Key notes

Chemistry 2017: Year 12 Module 5, Equilibrium and Acid Reactions. This video teaches precipitation prediction from reference Ksp values.
Syllabus dotpoint (NSW Chemistry Stage 6, 2017, Module 5):
"predict the formation of a precipitate given the standard reference values for Ksp"
Official 2017 course: https://www.nsw.gov.au/education-and-training/nesa/curriculum/science/chemistry-stage-6-2017

Prerequisite: Solubility rules, Q against K, Ksp expressions and concentration after mixing. Next: acid and base models in Module 6.
